raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Motivation

#45250 added `SGLANG_ZMQ_ALLOWED_PEERS`: TCP-bound IPC sockets admit only the listed peer addresses, and a multi-node data-parallel deployment lists the addresses of its own nodes. The check is on the source address of the incoming connection, and a plain `socket.connect("tcp://<peer>:<port>")` leaves the choice of source address to the kernel. On a host with several addresses, for example a container on host networking that owns one address of its own while the host has others, the kernel can pick an address that is not in the allowlist. ZAP then rejects the connection, and a PUSH socket with no admitted peer blocks forever on its first send, so the deployment hangs after start-up with no error. Connections to a peer on the same node keep working, because a connect to a local address uses that address as its source, which is why the hang shows up only across nodes.

## Modifications

- `python/sglang/srt/environ.py`: new `SGLANG_ZMQ_SOURCE_IP` (default unset), the source address for outgoing TCP IPC connects.
- `python/sglang/srt/utils/network.py`: new `zmq_connect(socket, endpoint)`. When `SGLANG_ZMQ_SOURCE_IP` is set and the endpoint is a TCP endpoint whose host is an IP literal of the same address family, it connects with libzmq's documented `tcp://<source_endpoint>;<endpoint>` form ([zmq_tcp(7)](https://libzmq.readthedocs.io/en/latest/zmq_tcp.html), "Connecting a socket"), here `tcp://<source>:0;<host>:<port>`, so the peer sees the pinned address. A hostname endpoint, an `ipc://` endpoint, an endpoint that already carries a source, a source of the other family, an invalid source, and an unset variable all connect exactly as before. `get_zmq_socket(..., bind=False)` now connects through it.
- `python/sglang/srt/managers/load_snapshot.py`: `ZmqLoadSnapshotWriter` connects through `zmq_connect` as well, since its reader is one of the allowlisting sockets.
- `test/registered/unit/utils/test_network.py` (new, `base-a-test-cpu`): the endpoint rewrite table above, and a regression test with real sockets: with an allowlist of `127.0.0.2`, a PUSH client connecting to a PULL from `get_zmq_socket` at `127.0.0.1` is not delivered, and the same client with `SGLANG_ZMQ_SOURCE_IP=127.0.0.2` is. The second case fails if `get_zmq_socket` goes back to a plain connect.

A multi-node deployment sets the variable on each node to that node's own allowlisted address, next to `SGLANG_ZMQ_ALLOWED_PEERS`. With the variable unset nothing changes. Every connect made through `get_zmq_socket(..., bind=False)` (the data-parallel controller's REQ socket, the multi-tokenizer PUSH sockets, the encoder-disaggregation sockets, the tracing PUSH socket) now goes through `zmq_connect`, so a deployment that sets the variable pins all of them, and the rewrite leaves `ipc://` endpoints alone. The KV-transfer sockets under `disaggregation/common/conn.py` call `connect` directly and are not touched.

## Accuracy Tests

Not applicable: no change to scheduling, model execution or outputs.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Not applicable: with the variable unset the only addition is one string check per connect.

On this head: `pytest test/registered/unit/utils/test_network.py` passes (3 tests, 7 subtests), and fails on the pinned-source case when the `get_zmq_socket` hunk is reverted; `test/registered/unit/managers/test_load_snapshot_backends.py` and `test_data_parallel_controller.py` pass (54 tests). `pre-commit run` on the four files passes.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations).
- [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

@@ -368,6 +368,8 @@ class Envs:
     SGLANG_LOG_PICKLE_IPC_OBJECTS = EnvBool(False)
     # Comma-separated peer IPs admitted by TCP-bound IPC sockets; empty admits all.
     SGLANG_ZMQ_ALLOWED_PEERS = EnvTuple(tuple())
+    # Source IP for outgoing TCP IPC connects, so an allowlisting peer sees it.
+    SGLANG_ZMQ_SOURCE_IP = EnvStr(None)
     SGLANG_USE_MESSAGE_QUEUE_BROADCASTER = EnvBool(True)
     SGLANG_TCP_STORE_PORT = EnvInt(29600)
     # Base port hint for ephemeral sockets (ZMQ, SHM broadcaster, etc.).

@@ -53,7 +53,11 @@
 
 from sglang.srt.environ import envs
 from sglang.srt.runtime_context import get_parallel, get_serving
-from sglang.srt.utils.network import is_zmq_endpoint_ipv6, restrict_zmq_peers
+from sglang.srt.utils.network import (
+    is_zmq_endpoint_ipv6,
+    restrict_zmq_peers,
+    zmq_connect,
+)
 
 logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)
 
@@ -401,7 +405,7 @@ def __init__(
             self._socket.setsockopt(_zmq.IPV6, 1)
         self._socket.setsockopt(_zmq.LINGER, 0)
         self._socket.setsockopt(_zmq.CONFLATE, 1)
-        self._socket.connect(endpoint)
+        zmq_connect(self._socket, endpoint)
 
     def write(self, snapshot: LoadSnapshot) -> None:
         if snapshot.dp_rank != self.dp_rank:

@@ -468,11 +468,41 @@ def get_zmq_socket(
                 restrict_zmq_peers(context, socket)
             socket.bind(endpoint)
         else:
-            socket.connect(endpoint)
+            zmq_connect(socket, endpoint)
 
         return socket
 
 
+def zmq_connect(socket: zmq.Socket, endpoint: str) -> None:
+    """Connect `socket`, pinning TCP connects to `SGLANG_ZMQ_SOURCE_IP`.
+
+    `restrict_zmq_peers` admits peers by source address. On a host with
+    several addresses (e.g. a container on host networking) the kernel may
+    pick a source outside the allowlist, and a rejected PUSH blocks forever.
+    The pin uses libzmq's `tcp://<source_endpoint>;<endpoint>` form, zmq_tcp(7).
+    """
+    socket.connect(_with_source_ip(endpoint))
+
+
+def _with_source_ip(endpoint: str) -> str:
+    from sglang.srt.environ import envs
+
+    source = envs.SGLANG_ZMQ_SOURCE_IP.get()
+    if not source or not endpoint.startswith("tcp://") or ";" in endpoint:
+        return endpoint
+    address = endpoint[len("tcp://") :]
+    host = address.rsplit(":", 1)[0].strip("[]")
+    try:
+        source_ip, host_ip = ipaddress.ip_address(source), ipaddress.ip_address(host)
+    except ValueError:
+        return endpoint
+    # A source of the other family cannot reach the host.
+    if source_ip.version != host_ip.version:
+        return endpoint
+    source_host = f"[{source_ip}]" if source_ip.version == 6 else str(source_ip)
+    return f"tcp://{source_host}:0;{address}"
+
+
 def is_zmq_endpoint_ipv6(endpoint: str) -> bool:
     """Return whether a ZMQ TCP endpoint contains a bracketed IPv6 host."""
     prefix = "tcp://["

@@ -0,0 +1,78 @@
+"""Unit tests for srt/utils/network.py: ZMQ peer allowlist and source pinning."""
+
+import unittest
+
+import zmq
+
+from sglang.srt.environ import envs
+from sglang.srt.utils import network
+from sglang.test.ci.ci_register import register_cpu_ci
+from sglang.test.test_utils import CustomTestCase
+
+register_cpu_ci(est_time=10, suite="base-a-test-cpu")
+
+
+class TestZmqSourceIpEndpoint(CustomTestCase):
+    def test_rewrites_only_matching_tcp_ip_endpoints(self):
+        """`SGLANG_ZMQ_SOURCE_IP` is spliced in with libzmq's `src:0;dst` form;
+        hostnames, ipc endpoints and the other address family pass unchanged."""
+        cases = [
+            ("10.0.0.5", "tcp://10.0.0.1:5555", "tcp://10.0.0.5:0;10.0.0.1:5555"),
+            (
+                "2001:db8::2",
+                "tcp://[2001:db8::1]:5555",
+                "tcp://[2001:db8::2]:0;[2001:db8::1]:5555",
+            ),
+            ("2001:db8::2", "tcp://127.0.0.1:5555", "tcp://127.0.0.1:5555"),
+            ("10.0.0.5", "tcp://somehost:5555", "tcp://somehost:5555"),
+            ("10.0.0.5", "ipc:///tmp/sock", "ipc:///tmp/sock"),
+            (
+                "10.0.0.5",
+                "tcp://10.0.0.9:0;10.0.0.1:5555",
+                "tcp://10.0.0.9:0;10.0.0.1:5555",
+            ),
+            (None, "tcp://10.0.0.1:5555", "tcp://10.0.0.1:5555"),
+        ]
+        for source, endpoint, expected in cases:
+            with self.subTest(source=source, endpoint=endpoint):
+                with envs.SGLANG_ZMQ_SOURCE_IP.override(source):
+                    if source is None:
+                        envs.SGLANG_ZMQ_SOURCE_IP.clear()
+                    self.assertEqual(network._with_source_ip(endpoint), expected)
+
+
+class TestZmqAllowlistAdmitsPinnedSource(CustomTestCase):
+    """A multi-homed client whose kernel picks a source address outside the
+    peer allowlist is rejected and its PUSH blocks; pinning the source to the
+    allowlisted address must get the message through."""
+
+    def _delivered(self, source: str | None) -> bool:
+        server_ctx, client_ctx = zmq.Context(), zmq.Context()
+        try:
+            with envs.SGLANG_ZMQ_ALLOWED_PEERS.override("127.0.0.2"):
+                port, server = network.get_zmq_socket(server_ctx, zmq.PULL)
+                with envs.SGLANG_ZMQ_SOURCE_IP.override(source):
+                    if source is None:
+                        envs.SGLANG_ZMQ_SOURCE_IP.clear()
+                    client = network.get_zmq_socket(
+                        client_ctx, zmq.PUSH, f"tcp://127.0.0.1:{port}", bind=False
+                    )
+            client.send(b"ping")
+            return server.poll(2000) != 0
+        finally:
+            with network._zmq_authenticators_lock:
+                auth = network._zmq_authenticators.pop(server_ctx.underlying, None)
+            if auth is not None:
+                auth.stop()
+            server_ctx.destroy(linger=0)
+            client_ctx.destroy(linger=0)
+
+    def test_unpinned_connect_is_rejected(self):
+        self.assertFalse(self._delivered(None))
+
+    def test_pinned_connect_is_admitted(self):
+        self.assertTrue(self._delivered("127.0.0.2"))
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    unittest.main()
